title: Hosted API P0 Streaming Oscillation - runbook draft and incident review
synopsis: On 2027-10-25 we experienced a P0 outage impacting hosted API streaming sessions. Clients experienced intermittent stream termination and long tail response latency. Error rate across streaming routes spiked to ~18% 5xx for a 35-minute window; non-streaming routes saw increased p95 latency due to acceptor-saturation. This document captures an incident review plus an initial runbook draft for the specific failure mode.
impact:
- Affected surface: streaming endpoints (event-stream, chunked-generation) across us-west1 and us-east1 regions.
- Duration: ~35 minutes (2027-10-25 14:03 UTC -> 14:38 UTC)
- Observed metrics: 18% 5xx rate on streaming routes at peak, global p95 latency for generation rose from 320ms to 12s for ~22 minutes.
- Customers: ~400k streaming tokens affected, 78 customers reported degraded UX, 5 automated monitoring clients retried aggressively leading to increased load.
- Business: Several PLG customers saw degraded chat experiences; no data loss reported because sessions were resumable once streams reconnected.
timeline:
2027-10-25 14:01 UTC - Spike alert: streaming-5xx-rate > 10% (alert SRE-STREAM-5XX).
2027-10-25 14:03 UTC - On-call paged; initial hypothesis: edge TLS session rehandshake causing drop.
2027-10-25 14:08 UTC - SREs observed acceptor thread pool saturation on the streaming proxy nodes; high backlog in multiplex queue.
2027-10-25 14:12 UTC - Deployed temporary traffic-shedding rule to reduce new streaming session acceptance at frontend (throttle to 30%).
2027-10-25 14:18 UTC - Engineering discovered duplicate EOF/RESET sequence patterns in gRPC transport logs correlated with RDMA-enabled transport (new in last rollout).
2027-10-25 14:22 UTC - Disabled RDMA transport for streaming routes via config flag; immediate drop in duplicate EOF events.
2027-10-25 14:26 UTC - Gradual rollback of traffic-shedding; acceptor backlog reduced, 5xx rate falling.
2027-10-25 14:38 UTC - Metrics stabilized to baseline.
2027-10-25 15:05 UTC - Post-incident call to capture initial notes and assign follow-ups.
detection_and_alerting: Detection triggered by existing SRE-STREAM-5XX alert rule (5xx rate over 5m window). Secondary signals: client reconnect spikes, acceptor backlog > 90th percentile, and a new internal error metric 'stream_transport_reset' spiking. Observability gaps noted: we lacked a dedicated metric for duplicate EOF events and for 'session-resync' occurrence count; these were surfaced by deep log inspection rather than metric alerting.
root_cause: Interaction bug between the streaming multiplexer and the RDMA-enabled gRPC transport. Under load, certain RDMA path reordering produced duplicate EOF/RESET frames which the multiplexer treated as end-of-stream followed by immediate session-resync attempts. The resync path uses an exclusive acceptor handshake that temporarily holds the acceptor thread and stalls new multiplexed connections. A feedback loop formed: retries increased backlog, backlog caused more transport reorders/timeouts, more resyncs triggered, leading to acceptor pool saturation and 5xx/latency amplification.
immediate_mitigations:
- Disable RDMA transport flag for streaming routes (rolled back new transport) -> reduced duplicate EOF events.
- Apply temporary throttle on new streaming sessions at frontend (30% throttle) to prevent acceptor saturation.
- Increase acceptor pool size by +50% on streaming proxy fleet as a short-term capacity buffer.
- Add emergency circuit-breaker to drop immediate resync attempts if acceptor backlog > 75%.
rollback_and_containment: Primary containment was disabling RDMA transport and throttling new sessions. Disabling RDMA removed the trigger event (duplicate EOF). Throttling plus acceptor pool increase prevented re-saturation while teams prepared a targeted patch. No further rollbacks to customer-facing features were needed.
long_term_remediations:
- Fix: update multiplexer EOF handling to idempotently handle duplicate EOF/RESET sequences (runtime PR in progress).
- Transport-layer: add stricter frame-sequencing checks and telemetry for RDMA path reordering.
- Runbook/automation: add automated emergency flag to globally disable RDMA for streaming if 'duplicate-eof' metric spikes.
- Testing: add deterministic chaos tests that inject duplicate EOF/RESET at transport layer and validate multiplexer behavior under load.
- Capacity: make acceptor scaling reactive to session-resync rate and add soft quota for aggressive client retries.
- Observability: create a dedicated metric 'stream_duplicate_eof_count' and an alert (>50 in 1m) and dashboard panel.
- Post-deploy checklist: any transport change must run the new chaos test suite and pass the streaming multiplexer gating tests before rollout to production.
runbook_draft:
1) Alert triage: verify SRE-STREAM-5XX alert and check 'stream_duplicate_eof_count' (if present).
2) Immediate action: if duplicate EOF events detected, flip RDMA-streaming-disable flag (config manager: feature.rdma_streaming=false).
3) Throttle: apply streaming-session accept rate limit to 30% at edge via traffic-control or fleet gate.
4) Capacity buffer: scale acceptor pool +50% on streaming proxies.
5) Circuit breaker: enable resync-suppression (if acceptor_backlog_pct > 75 -> suppress resync attempts for 30s).
6) Observe: monitor 5xx rate, acceptor backlog, and client reconnect rate; wait for 2 consecutive 5m windows below threshold.
7) Rollback: once stable, re-enable traffic gradually and remove throttles.
8) Post-incident: snapshot logs and collect transport traces for RCA.
9) If steps 2-4 have no effect within 10m, escalate to SRE lead and transport eng oncall.

notes_for_oncall:
- If you see acceptor_pool_backlog_pct > 80% and stream_transport_reset spikes, immediately consider disabling RDMA transport flag.
- Prefer temporary throttles over broad rollback of runtimes; throttles are safer and faster.
- Preserve a log bundle from the first 20 minutes for engineering (they contain transport traces useful for replay).
- Use the emergency-runbook channel and tag transport-eng for rapid coordination.
